title: Build the oak frame hut with axis-correct log posts
goal: On a fresh judged 1.19.2 server, reproduce the sealed 17-block Oak Frame Hut: four two-high oak_log corner posts that must verify with vertical (y) axis orientation, plus a 3x3 oak_planks roof. The judger's block check compares the placed log axis against the blueprint, so a log placed sideways scores as a miss even though the block id matches; plan placements that guarantee the axis, verify each post against the judger snapshot feed, and re-place anything that scans wrong. Finish with block_hit_rate 1.0 in the judger's own result ledger while keeping the required action and token ledgers current.
resources: docker image itzg/minecraft-server:2024.6.1-java17 (Minecraft 1.19.2 vanilla; compose file assets/gc-361/docker-compose.yml)
docker image node:20.15.1 (Node 20 runtime for mineflayer bots and the judger's JS bridge)
process_expectations: The plan artifact names the axis-placement tactic for each of the 8 log positions before execution
Verification commands against data/score.json snapshots actually ran between placement batches (present in the run log with timestamps)
Each axis mismatch is tracked by identity (coordinate + expected axis + scanned axis) and its fix is re-verified in a later snapshot
Honest ledgers: action_log.json intervals match the bot's real connect/build windows; tokens.json records actual LLM spend
